provenance.note: Four reviewed Gram Panchayat briefs for Thanjavur (Poondi, Kuruvikkarambai, Vettuvakkottai, Nanjikkottai), written by hand from the July 2026 four-Panchayat slice and its shared evidence record (docs/research/thanjavur-four-panchayat-slice-2026-07.md). A reviewed brief carries what a person understood about the place and is preferred by the Panchayat page over the generated brief of the same LGD code, which stays underneath for the named gaps. The closed sources are the documents read once for these four places: the AgriNet crop rows and the Bhuvan counts are dated one-time readings, not feeds, and are not re-acquired. Groundwater figures here are the 2024 FIRKA assessment read from the CGWB report; the generated briefs use the IN-GRES TALUK assessment, so the two can legitimately differ for the same place.

conventions.precedence: a curated brief overrides the generated brief of the same lgdCode on the page; nothing here is machine-derived
conventions.reviewedAt: the date the reviewer checked identity and evidence; the page shows it beside the brief
conventions.groundwater: firka-level (2024 CGWB report), containing-area context, not a Panchayat measurement

briefs.name: Poondi
briefs.thesis: Recorded tap-water coverage and a historically canal-dependent farm landscape now sit within a semi-critical groundwater setting.
briefs.verdictTitle: Drinking-water service is well documented; present-day irrigation reliability is not.
briefs.verdictBody: JJM lists a tap connection for every recorded household and recent programme sampling. Census records show strong historical dependence on canals, while Saliyamangalam firka is classified Semi Critical. The missing link is current irrigation: the available records do not show whether today’s paddy area receives dependable canal water or is shifting pressure onto groundwater.

insights.title: Administrative identity
insights.text: Poondi is recorded as LGD Gram Panchayat 228400 and JJM Gram Panchayat 152086; the Census record covers settlements 638660 and 638661.

insights.title: Drinking-water service
insights.text: JJM displays 1,143 households and 1,143 tap connections across three habitations, eight deep-tubewell source rows, 94 sample rows, and a latest displayed Safe sample dated 2026-07-16.

insights.title: Land and irrigation baseline
insights.text: The 2009 Census baseline totals 711.53 ha, 438.98 ha net sown, and 432.97 ha irrigated; 425.08 ha of the irrigated area is recorded as canal irrigation.

insights.title: Current crop signal
insights.text: Summer 2025 AgriNet rows show 332.2 ha across Poondi-1 and Poondi-2, chiefly paddy, but current irrigation method remains unknown.

insights.title: Groundwater pressure
insights.text: Saliyamangalam firka is Semi Critical at 85.8 percent in the 2024 groundwater assessment.

nextEvidence: Which canal and command area currently serve Poondi?
Which nearby rain gauge best represents local seasonal conditions?
How much of today’s cultivated area depends on canals, wells, or both?
Where do the Panchayat boundary, drainage paths, flood-prone areas, and water bodies lie?

briefs.name: Kuruvikkarambai
briefs.thesis: A large coconut-growing area and recorded tap-water coverage sit within an over-exploited groundwater setting.
briefs.verdictTitle: Coconut cultivation and groundwater pressure need closer local monitoring.
briefs.verdictBody: Summer 2025 crop records show a large coconut footprint, Census records show substantial historical canal irrigation, and JJM lists a sizeable groundwater-based drinking-water system. Kuruvikkarambai firka is Over Exploited. These facts justify closer water-use monitoring, but they do not show the current irrigation source, field method, delivery schedule, or crop stress needed for farm advice.

insights.title: Administrative identity
insights.text: Kuruvikkarambai is recorded as LGD Gram Panchayat 228711 and JJM Gram Panchayat 152422; its service and Census records cover two settlements.

insights.title: Drinking-water service
insights.text: JJM displays 1,566 households and connections across ten habitations and a combined service population of 6,370; it lists 29 deep-tubewell source rows.

insights.title: Land and irrigation baseline
insights.text: The 2009 Census baseline totals 1,251.74 ha, 874.22 ha net sown, and 253.29 ha irrigated, including 241.50 ha by canals.

insights.title: Current crop signal
insights.text: Summer 2025 AgriNet rows show 823.1 ha across Kuruvikkarambai-1 and -2, dominated by coconut, but do not identify the current irrigation source or delivery system.

insights.title: Groundwater pressure
insights.text: Kuruvikkarambai firka is Over Exploited at 121.9 percent in the 2024 groundwater assessment.

briefs.name: Vettuvakkottai
briefs.thesis: A mixed canal-and-well irrigation history meets over-exploited groundwater and a dated direct-to-water-body drainage signal.
briefs.verdictTitle: A historic drainage warning deserves verification—not a pollution label.
briefs.verdictBody: Historical records show substantial irrigation split between canals and wells, while Summer 2025 records show a mixed crop portfolio. A 2009 Census record for Ooranipuram says drainage discharged directly to a water body. This should prompt a present-day check; it does not establish current contamination or identify a pollution source.

insights.title: Administrative identity
insights.text: Vettuvakkottai is recorded as LGD Gram Panchayat 228911 and JJM Gram Panchayat 152334; its Census record covers settlements 638954, 638955, and 638956.

insights.title: Drinking-water service
insights.text: JJM displays 742 households and connections across nine habitations, 23 deep-tubewell source rows, and a latest displayed Safe sample dated 2026-06-29.

insights.title: Land and irrigation baseline
insights.text: The 2009 Census baseline totals 1,202.68 ha, 794.92 ha net sown, and 629.83 ha irrigated, split between 348.00 ha by canals and 281.83 ha by wells.

insights.title: Dated pollution-pressure signal
insights.text: Ooranipuram's 2009 amenity record says drainage discharged directly to a water body. This is a historical warning that requires a present-day check, not a current pollution finding.

insights.title: Agriculture and groundwater
insights.text: Summer 2025 AgriNet shows 138.4 ha across a mixed crop portfolio; Kavalipatti firka is Over Exploited at 126.7 percent.

nextEvidence: Does the recorded drainage outlet still discharge to the same water body?
What do current water-quality measurements show at the outlet and receiving water?
How much irrigation currently depends on canals compared with wells?
Where are the Panchayat boundary, drains, farms, and receiving water body?

briefs.name: Nanjikkottai
briefs.thesis: A large peri-urban Census Town combines extensive drinking-water records with severe groundwater pressure across its firka.
briefs.verdictTitle: Extensive tap-water service sits alongside severe groundwater pressure.
briefs.verdictBody: JJM displays tap connections for 9,512 households, with supply records spanning deep tubewells and lake sources. At the same time, the containing Nanjikottai firka is classified Over Exploited, with groundwater extraction assessed at 122.4 percent. The public record establishes the scale of service and groundwater pressure, but not whether supply is continuous, seasonally reliable, or environmentally safe.

insights.title: Administrative identity
insights.text: This profile covers Nanjikottai Census Town under Nanjikkottai Gram Panchayat; its official administrative and service identifiers are listed below.

insights.title: Population and settlements
insights.text: TNRD's Census 2011 table records 32,689 people for Nanjikottai, while JJM displays a service population of 35,135; the different vintages and programme definitions do not support a growth calculation.

insights.title: Drinking-water service
insights.text: JJM displays 9,512 households and connections across 24 habitations, 30 deep-tubewell and 39 lake source rows, and 714 sample rows with a latest displayed Safe sample dated 2026-07-18.

insights.title: Public works evidence
insights.text: Bhuvan lists 333 accepted geotags, including 152 water-adjacent programme records. The counts do not establish that every record is a separate asset, or that each asset is functional and currently maintained.

insights.title: Groundwater pressure
insights.text: Nanjikottai firka is Over Exploited at 122.4 percent in the 2024 groundwater assessment.

nextEvidence: What are the current crop area, irrigation sources, and agricultural water demand?
How many of the recorded lake sources and public works are distinct and functional?
What do current water-quality measurements show in local lakes, drains, and supply sources?
Where is the current Panchayat boundary in relation to Thanjavur Corporation?
